s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden collapse with ventricular fibrillation and subsequent coma
key_facts: 21-year-old woman with autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability
On risperidone
No prior history of syncope, cardiac arrest, or known cardiovascular disease
Family denied any illicit drug or alcohol use
Witnessed collapse at a noisy auto mechanic shop
Bystander ECG showed ventricular fibrillation
Return of spontaneous circulation achieved after two defibrillations
Blood pressure 93/70 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, and oxygen saturation 100% on arrival
Intravenous amiodarone infusion and oral amiodarone administered
Normal chemistry panel and electrolytes
Initial electrocardiogram revealed sinus rhythm with interpolated premature ventricular complexes
Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated ejection fraction of 45-50%, normal wall thickness, and no valvular abnormalities

differentials: Ventricular fibrillation due to coronary artery anomaly
per_call: Ventricular fibrillation due to coronary artery anomaly

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Witnessed collapse with ventricular fibrillation, normal heart structure on echocardiogram

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Ventricular fibrillation and reduced ejection fraction, possible right ventricular involvement

shortlist.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Ejection fraction of 45-50% and normal wall thickness, possible dilated cardiomyopathy

shortlist.label: Risperidone-induced QT prolongation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient on risperidone, which can cause QT prolongation and increase risk of ventricular fibrillation

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Reduced ejection fraction and ventricular fibrillation, possible myocardial inflammation

raw.rationale: The patient's witnessed collapse at a noisy auto mechanic shop, bystander ECG showing ventricular fibrillation, and the presence of interpolated premature ventricular complexes on the initial electrocardiogram are consistent with catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, which is often triggered by emotional or physical stress.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated normal wall thickness and no valvular abnormalities, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Although the ejection fraction was 45-50%, the wall thickness was normal, which does not support a diagnosis of dilated cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Risperidone-induced QT prolongation
rejected.why: The initial electrocardiogram did not show QT prolongation, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Myocarditis
rejected.why: There is no mention of symptoms or laboratory findings consistent with myocarditis, such as fever, chest pain, or elevated troponin levels.
